Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

dazdiff 0.1.0

First release.

  • diff_table() compares two tables value by value, returning a data.table with one row per compared value, traceable to its source row in both inputs (row_id_x, row_id_y), and a status of same, changed, only_x or only_y.
  • Two modes:
    • mode = "benchmark" (the default) tests y against the benchmark x. y’s columns are cast to x’s types, its extra columns are dropped with a message, and a column it lacks is an error.
    • mode = "equal" compares the two as peers. Every column must be in both tables with the same type, nothing is cast, and the result is symmetric.
  • exclude leaves columns out of the comparison, in either mode: they are removed from both tables, in either spelling, before anything else. A name in neither table is a warning, so one list of technical columns can serve many tables.
  • A number of y cast to the benchmark’s text is written with the decimals the benchmark uses, when they are the same for the whole column, so 2 meets "2.0", and a message says so (dazdiff_message_cast_format). A number that still matches only by value, not by text, is a warning (dazdiff_warning_cast_format) that explains the format used.
  • When no key aligns, the error names the key columns that share no value between the tables, with examples, and suggests exclude for those holding one value in each table.
  • Casts that drop a fraction – a double to an integer, a number or a timestamp to a whole day, a Date holding part of a day to its text – are made by default, since storage such as Spark or Delta narrows types the same way. Each one is announced and recorded; truncate = FALSE refuses them.
  • A timestamp cast to text is always written "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", midnight included, with its fraction of a second (to the microsecond) when it has one, so the text does not depend on the values or the R version.
  • A logical column of nothing but NA, which is how read.csv() and fread() type a column with no values, casts to any type, a Date included.
  • Column names in both tables are normalized to upper-case letters, digits and _, so amount and Amount are one column. Letters outside ASCII are kept. Two names in one table that normalize to the same thing are an error.
  • by names the row identity. measures chooses the compared columns, by type ("numeric", "numeric+integer") or by name. With no measures, diff_table() compares whole rows.
  • A table must have at least one key column. When it has none, row_key = "position" adds the row number as a virtual key, and row_key = "sorted" adds it after sorting both tables by their values, so row order does not matter.
  • Duplicate keys are paired in arrival order with a warning, compared as exact multisets with duplicates = "aggregate", or refused with duplicates = "error".
  • nan_is_na = TRUE treats NaN as NA, in values and in key columns alike.
  • A comparison in which no row aligns is an error, not a report of two unrelated tables.
  • rel_tol adds a relative tolerance to the absolute tolerance: a value is same when it is within either. The relative difference is taken against the larger magnitude of the two values, so it is symmetric, and both tolerances apply to finite pairs only. The result carries abs_diff and rel_diff beside diff, diff_summary() reports max_rel_diff, and the tolerances are recorded in attr(, "tolerance").
  • diff_report() draws a bounded text report of a comparison: the columns compared, a picture of how the rows of the two tables align, and per measure its match rate and largest differences. The layout follows the summary of the Python package diffly.
  • diff_explain() says which key values split the result into same and not same: per key column (and per measure), how many of its values only match, only differ or are mixed, and, for one column, the status counts of each value. among = "joined" explains the changed values alone.
  • is_matching() answers TRUE or FALSE: do the two tables match? With tolerance or rel_tol it re-judges the stored differences at other thresholds, looser or stricter, without running the comparison again.
  • diff_summary() counts each status per measure and measures the size of the differences.
  • expect_table_equal() is a testthat expectation built on diff_table(). It allows a relative difference of sqrt(.Machine$double.eps) by default, as testthat’s expect_equal() does, where diff_table() is exact. Duplicate keys are an error unless duplicates accepts them, and tables that share no key fail the expectation.
  • compare_columns() shows how the columns of two tables line up, normalize_dt() converts other types (factors, timestamps, integer64) to the ones diff_table() compares, and cast_rules() lists the conversions it makes. A factor becomes its labels by default, and the mappings given in normalize_dt(to = ) are added to that default.
  • Every error, warning and message has a class, listed under Conditions in ?diff_table.
